lines: Taylor Nguyen
+1 (555) 010-6642 | taylor.nguyen@example.com | example.com/code/tnguyen
EDUCATION
Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Jul 2023 - Aug 2024
- Owned the department websites and the shared component library other developers relied on.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; the findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Wrote the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Improved page performance by 35% by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Wrote 60 component tests for the search filters, which caught 3 regressions before release.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Prevented cross-site scripting in comments by storing user input in React state before rendering it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cached the stop list offline, so the app opened in 0.8s on a slow 3G connection against 2.9s before.
- Open-sourced the app, and the city transit agency linked it from its developer page.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Rebuilt a travel search page with server rendering, more than halving its load time and lifting bookings by about a tenth.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybok, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: The Experience section is not ordered newest first.
items.because: The older Westfield role appears above the Lumen internship, making the timeline harder to scan and hiding the most recent experience.

items.says: The move from Web Developer to Frontend Engineering Intern can read as a seniority step backward.
The line states responsibility without showing what changed as a result.
items.because: A hiring manager cannot distinguish routine maintenance from work that improved the websites or delivery.

items.says: “Owned” does not identify the technical work performed.
items.because: It frames the work as a duty rather than a concrete implementation contribution.

items.says: The sentence makes the findings, rather than you, the actor.
items.because: “The findings led to” obscures whether you designed or implemented the preview mode.

items.says: The strongest bullet in the Westfield entry is not first.
items.because: Leading with a responsibility-only bullet delays the clearest user-facing result.

items.says: The accessibility checklist does not identify its standard or criteria.
The figures do not specify whether 12 and 2 count audits, pages, or findings.
items.because: Those units represent very different scales of improvement.

items.says: The comparison omits the unit after “under 1.”
items.because: The missing unit makes the measurement read as incomplete.

items.says: “Search time” does not identify the performance metric compared.
items.because: Response latency, result-render time, and task-completion time measure different things.

items.says: The 35% improvement lacks a performance metric and comparison baseline.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what improved or evaluate the scale of the change.

items.says: The repeated “by” makes the cause-and-result phrasing clunky.
Lazy-loading the hero image cannot credibly explain the claimed Largest Contentful Paint reduction.
items.because: Lazy-loading an above-the-fold hero generally delays its request and worsens LCP.

items.says: The metric name uses incorrect capitalization.
items.because: Largest Contentful Paint is the metric’s official name.

items.says: Storing untrusted input in React state does not prevent cross-site scripting when rendering it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
items.because: React state neither sanitizes nor escapes attacker-controlled HTML.

items.says: The definitive XSS-prevention claim has no verification result.
The Lumen entry’s strongest result is not its opening bullet.
items.because: This bullet establishes technical and commercial impact faster than the opening performance percentage.

items.says: The live-arrival claim does not say how transit data was retrieved or refreshed.
The weekly adoption figure does not define “riders” or give its source.
“Opened” does not define the loading milestone measured at 0.8 seconds.
items.because: Different milestones describe different user experiences.

items.says: The offline-caching claim does not identify its implementation mechanism.
“Against 2.9s before” phrases the before-and-after comparison awkwardly.
items.because: It slows comprehension and makes the reduction sound unnatural.

items.says: “Open-sourced” does not show what made the project understandable or reusable.
The agency link does not show what the exposure changed.
items.because: It establishes recognition but not whether it generated users, referrals, or contributions.

items.says: The bullet says React and TypeScript, contradicting the entry’s Vue header.
items.because: The conflicting framework labels make the implementation unclear.

items.says: “Worked on” does not identify the capability you delivered.
items.because: A reader cannot tell which booking step you implemented or what users could do because of it.

items.says: “Handling” does not explain the calendar’s behavior for the named edge cases.
items.because: It does not say whether the component prevented conflicts, detected overlaps, or converted displayed times.

items.says: The calendar-ownership bullet should lead the entry.
items.because: It shows more specific ownership than the current opening statement.

items.says: The modifier does not make clear whether the component, the tests, or both handled the edge cases.
The travel-search accomplishment is in the wrong entry and duplicates the Lumen result.
items.because: Travel search and booking conversion do not fit the library hackathon, and the close match makes attribution unclear.

items.says: The result lacks a load-time metric and a basis for comparing bookings.
items.because: Load milestones differ, and booking changes need a defined denominator or experiment.

items.says: The bullet places its strongest outcomes after the implementation detail.
items.because: The load-time and booking results have more scanning value than the server-rendering method.

items.says: “Storybok” is misspelled.
items.because: The typo can look careless on a technical résumé and prevent an exact keyword match.
